newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton settles higher in rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton settles higher in rangebound trade.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed a dull session slightly firmer, buoyed by speculative shortcovering, dealers said.

While some analysts viewed the gains as a temporary correction to recent losses and said further weakness is in store, others said the market is due for a sharp correction to the upside once the May contract expires.
Support was pegged at 72.00 cents in July, below the life-of-contract low of 72.05 cents.
Open interest in May remained high at 14,493 lots, down 2,526 lots as of Friday's close, with the first notice day for the spot month on Thursday.
"It all hinges on exports," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said. "If we continue to see Chinese buying interest there is no reason why the market should continue to drift lower."
July finished 0.41 cent per lb firmer at 72.90 cents, having ranged from 73.00 to 72.49 cents per lb. Spot May closed 0.28 cent higher at 71.08 cents.
Volume was estimated at 17,000 lots compared with Monday's official 11,492 lots.
